title: World Bank warns of AI concentration risks as it lifts East Asia and Pacific growth outlook to 4.5%
source_used: UA.NEWS summary of the CNBC report; Crypto Briefing summary on TradingView; the World Bank's own Executive Summary of the East Asia and Pacific Economic Update, October 2026 (openknowledge.worldbank.org). CNBC original not opened (HTTP 403).
key_facts: The World Bank raised its 2026 growth forecast for East Asia and the Pacific to 4.5%, 0.3 percentage points higher than it expected in April; growth slows to 4.4% in 2027 and 4.3% in 2028 (23 economies).
Vietnam got the largest upgrade among major economies, up 1.1 points to 7.4%; Malaysia 5.1%; China 4.4%; Philippines unchanged at 3.7% (Crypto Briefing summary).

AI-related goods made up more than half of export growth in most of the region's economies and more than 70% in Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam; trade growth excluding them was weak or negative.
China, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam exported $1.4 trillion of AI-related goods in the 12 months through April.
The bank warned of a downturn in global technology spending; AI capital spending has reached about 6% of US GDP, similar to the 2000 peak in IT investment.

Of $2.9 trillion of AI investment planned for 2025-2028, about $800 billion could come from private credit; AI-related lending was 34% of private-credit activity in 2025 versus an 18% average over the previous five years; private credit is less transparent and untested by a serious downturn.

World Bank Executive Summary: the region's dependence on AI-related industrial activity 'could become a weakness if global AI activity slows or reverses'; high energy prices and an unusually strong El Nino are further risks.
quote_evidence: The World Bank has raised its forecast for economic growth in East Asia and the Pacific in 2026 to 4.5% — 0.3 percentage points higher than it expected in April.
In Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam, their share exceeded 70%.
The bank stressed that private credit markets are less transparent and have not yet been tested by a serious downturn.
why_it_matters_hint: A strong AI export boom is lifting regional growth, but the World Bank says reliance on it could become a weakness if global AI spending falls back.
notes: CNBC page blocked (HTTP 403). UA.NEWS states it summarises CNBC's report on the World Bank's new report; the Executive Summary of the report itself confirms the AI supply-chain boost, the 4.4% average for 2026-28 and the downside risk if global AI activity slows. The 4.5%, 0.3-point, 70% and private-credit figures come from the UA.NEWS/CNBC and Crypto Briefing summaries.
